To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the absolute number of bound activin ligand per cell is the signal for the concentration dependent transcriptional responses to activin and that a 3fold difference in the absolute amount of activin receptor ligand per cell leads only to a 3fold change in the amount of nuclear Smad2.
a 3-fold difference in the absolute concentration of activin in the extracellular environment is relayed directly as a 3-fold change in the amount of nuclear transduction protein, SMAD2.

the absolute number of activin receptors per cell determines the level of nuclear Smad2, which is in turn proportional to the level of activin in the cell, which is proportional to the activin concentration in the embryo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underlie morphogen gradient interpretation in Xenopus embryos.
how cells sense the concentration of a morphogen, in this case activin.
the mechanisms that underlie the interpretation of a morphogen concentration gradient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quantitative difference in the absolute amount of nuclear SMADD2 protein is the key to the differential gene response in the nucleus.
the absolute number of activated activin receptors per cell is a critical parameter for activin signal transduction.
the absolute number of activated receptors in a cell is the signal that determines the level of gene activation in response to a morphogen gradient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the quantitative differences in activin concentration are relayed to the nucleus by a quantitative difference in the number of occupied receptors, a quantitative difference in nuclear SMAD2 levels, and a quantitative difference in Xbra and XGSC gene transcription.

the quantitative differences in the number of activated activin receptors are relayed directly to a corresponding difference in the amount SMAD2 protein that is translocated to the nucleus and that this difference is sufficient to account for the qualitative differences in the gene response.

a 3-fold change in the absolute number or concentration of occupied receptors can be maintained as a 3-fold difference in the level or number of nuclear SMAD protein, which in turn is responsible for a 3-fold differential transcriptional response.
The main takeaway from our work is that

quantitative differences in the number of activated receptors are maintained as quantitative differences in the level of the transducer protein in the nucleus and that this is sufficient to account for the qualitative changes in gene expression.

the quantitative differences in the extracellular signal concentration are directly translated into quantitative differences in nuclear responses, and that the signal transduction process is highly efficient.

the quantitative differences in the number of receptors occupied by activin are maintained in the nucleus as quantitative differences in the level of SMAD2, and that this is the key step in morphogen gradient interpretation.
